stories.title: ‘I stand by it’: Chaudhry Salik sticks to Punjab corruption claims despite Maryam's ire
summary: Minister for Overseas Pakistanis and PML-Q leader Chaudhry Salik Hussain on Wednesday asserted that he stood by his claims regarding corruption in Punjab.

In response to a question, Salik said he had not been contacted by any government official or PML-N after the incident; except for an earlier meeting with Information Minister Attaullah Tarar during which he explained the context.

The PML-Q further argued that his interview in Lahore was recorded on Sept 25 — rather than earlier this month when the remarks surfaced — while the DC was appointed on Oct 31. “The Punjab chief minister made these remarks based on incorrect information,” Salik said.

stories.title: 10 cops martyred, 18 terrorists killed as police party comes under attack in KP's Kohat
summary: PESHAWAR: Eighteen terrorists were killed while 10 cops were martyred on Wednesday when the police team came under attack on its way back after completing an operation against elements involved in illegal gold mining, police said.
Last month, a police officer was martyred after terrorists attacked a police post in KP’s Bajaur.
On Oct 7, seven policemen were injured when terrorists attacked a police checkpost in Kohat.

stories.title: PTI lawyers meet Imran, Bushra 'for 3 hours' at Adiala jail following IHC orders
summary: Barrister Safdar said on X that a “nearly three-hour-long meeting with Imran Khan [sahib] and Bushra Bibi was allowed” by jail authorities.

Safdar said that given the “extraordinary duration” of the meeting from 4-7pm, the legal and medical issues of both Imran and Bushra “were discussed in detail and comprehensive legal instructions were given by both”.
Speaking to Dawn earlier, PTI lawyer Awais Younus Chaudhry said the Safdar and Khosa’s meeting with Imran and Bushra was to “discuss under-trial cases”.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz highlights Pakistan's solar 'revolution by ordinary citizens' at COP31
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday highlighted Pakistan’s solar power boom at the COP31 in Turkiye, where world leaders gathered to discuss joint solutions to combat climate change.

In his speech at the Antalya Leaders’ Summit, PM Shehbaz will highlight Pakistan’s climate priorities and emphasise the urgent need for enhanced global climate action and strengthened international cooperation to mitigate the adverse impacts of climate change, according to PMO.
It is telling us to fight harder.” PM meets world leaders On the sidelines of the summit, the prime minister held conversations with leaders of various countries and international bodies.

stories.title: Nadra launches chatbot that tells families exact papers needed for succession certificates
summary: ISLAMABAD: Families dealing with inheritance can now get the exact process and list of documents for their case from an automated chatbot, introduced on the revamped succession website of the National Database and Registration Authority (Nadra).

The deceased must be in Nadra’s records and the heirs must be registered in the Family Registration Certificate (FRC), while the applicant must hold a valid CNIC, Nadra card or Pakistan Origin Card (POC), as the old manual NIC is no longer accepted.
If any condition is not fulfilled, Nadra does not issue the certificate and the family has to approach the court.

stories.title: JI announces nationwide protests, Lahore rally against inflation and delays in LG polls
summary: LAHORE: Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) emir Hafiz Naeemur Rehman on Wednesday announced a series of major public gatherings across the country as part of the party’s campaign against inflation, farmers’ problems and delays in local government (LG) elections.

Speaking on Wednesday, Rehman said his party has now decided to broaden that movement to include protests against rising prices of petroleum products and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), difficulties faced by farmers and delays in holding LG polls.
Rehman demanded that the government pass on the benefits of declining international oil prices to consumers while curbing excessive profits made by oil refineries.

stories.title: Iran slams 'repugnant' $20m US reward for nuclear information
summary: Iran hit out at the United States’ $20 million reward for information on its nuclear programme on Wednesday, calling it “repugnant and regrettable”.

US President Donald Trump has repeatedly said Iran’s nuclear programme was effectively obliterated by the brief US strikes on key Iranian nuclear facilities during the 12-day war between Iran and Israel in June 2025.
Araghchi previously said that talks over Iran’s nuclear programme would come at a later stage.

stories.title: Petrol drops by Rs3, diesel by Rs7 for Nov 12
summary: The federal government on Wednesday decreased the price of petrol by Rs3 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs7 per litre for November 12.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs335 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs364 per litre for Thursday.
The revision comes a day after the government slashed the price of petrol by Rs8 per litre and that of HSD by Rs7 per litre for November 11.

stories.title: 3 killed, 13 injured in collision of coach and motorcycle in KP's DI Khan
summary: DERA ISMAIL KHAN: Three people were killed and 13 others injured when a coach collided with a motorcycle in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Dera Ismail Khan on Wednesday, according to Rescue 1122.
Last week, at least eight people were killed and 30 others injured when a passenger bus collided with a dumptruck near the Havelian Interchange on KP’s Hazara Motorway.
The day before, a collision between a passenger bus and a truck claimed the lives of 11 people and left 33 others injured near Punjab’s Pakpattan.

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine say some progress made at talks, US cites a lack of trust
summary: Read: New round of US-brokered Russia-Ukraine peace talks starts in Abu Dhabi Despite public optimism from Trump, there has been no sign of major compromises on the main ​issues after more than 4-1/2 years of war since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

With talks deadlocked on land - Ukraine has rejected Russian President Vladimir Putin's demands to surrender the whole of ​the eastern region of Donbas in return for peace - US mediators have tried to steer talks toward post-war security guarantees and reconstruction.
European officials say wider security talks should only come after a ceasefire, ​and Russia should not be allowed to influence Europe's security arrangements or rewarded for starting the war.

stories.title: Centurions De Silva, Mendis foil Pakistan as Sri Lanka dig in
summary: Dhananjaya de Silva and Kusal Mendis showed great staying power as both posted centuries to lift Sri Lanka to 404-4 on day three of the first Test against Pakistan in Rawalpindi on Wednesday.

De Silva was unbeaten on a polished 167, while Mendis was 117 not out as the pair frustrated Pakistan in an unbroken fifth-wicket stand of 249, bringing Sri Lanka within 30 runs of the home team’s total of 434-9 declared.
Sri Lanka lost just one wicket in the first session of the day’s play as De Silva and Kamindu Mendis put on a 90 for the fourth wicket, ensuring Sri Lanka built up from an overnight total of 114-3.

stories.title: CT battle
summary: What is important is for operations against violent anti-state elements to continue so that these groups are rooted out for good.

While the Taliban are reluctant to cooperate against terrorists who launch attacks on Pakistan from Afghan soil, the state here must do all possible to ensure violent elements have no safe spaces within our borders.
This time the state should ensure that after the terrorism-hit areas are cleared, the government builds on the gains so that local people can live in peace.

stories.title: Security breach case: SC disposes of Imaan Mazari, husband’s petition as infructuous
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Supreme Court on Wednesday disposed of a petition filed by lawyers Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha, as infructuous, directing the Islamabad High Court (IHC) to decide on a petition filed by the couple in the security breach case.

On Oct 29, an Islamabad anti-terrorism court (ATC) sentenced the couple to 10 years in prison each in the security breach case, pertaining to the disruption of an international cricket team’s security route and incitement to public unrest.
Imaan and Hadi were also sentenced to two years each under Section 353 (assault or criminal force to deter public servant from discharge of his duty) of the PPC.

stories.title: What my mother’s death in Lahore taught me about patient care
summary: On one occasion, I was told: “You are not helping your mother but causing problems.” There were occasions when I felt that asking questions was interpreted as challenging authority rather than as an attempt by a family member to participate appropriately in her care.
The burden placed on the family At one point, the consultant instructed that my mother should receive two bags of blood.

I understand that critically ill patients require frequent monitoring and investigations but should the frequency, timing and necessity not be balanced against my mother’s age, physical condition, discomfort and overall clinical needs?

stories.title: Indonesia's vice president has resigned, aide says, stoking political uncertainty
summary: Indonesia's Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka has resigned, an aide said on Wednesday, a move that threatens ​to split a key political alliance and risks further political uncertainty in Southeast Asia's largest economy.

Gibran, the 39-year-old son of former President Joko ‌Widodo, has come under intense scrutiny from lawmakers following Constitutional Court and Supreme Court rulings last month that his education documents did not meet election requirements.
Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka has reportedly resigned, with Projo Chairman Budi Arie Setiadi confirming the submission of his resignation letter to President Prabowo Subianto.

stories.title: Former Afghan army member arrested for alleged terrorist activities in Pakistan
summary: PESHAWAR: Security forces and law enforcement agencies have arrested a man formerly associated with the Afghan National Army (ANA) for allegedly carrying out terrorist activities in Pakistan, it emerged on Wednesday.

For their part, the Afghan Taliban have avoided taking a categorical position on the TTP and other groups, while rejecting Islamabad’s allegations that Afghanistan is being used as a base for attacks against Pakistan.
It was also reported that the Afghan Taliban engaged in unprovoked firing the night before near Kurram as security forces foiled an attempt by terrorists to cross into Pakistan.

stories.title: Asian Development Bank approves $500m loan to help Pakistan strengthen disaster preparedness
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) on Wednesday approved contingent disaster financing (CDF) facilities up to $500 million for Pakistan to withstand disasters and facilitate disaster response.

The findings came in the wake of devastating 2025 floods, which submerged entire districts, displaced millions, and wiped out livelihoods, exposing critical gaps in preparedness despite years of policy frameworks, institutional reforms, and international commitments.
The report argued that reliance on reactive disaster management has proven insufficient in the face of intensifying climate stress.

stories.title: JI to continue protests nationwide as it demands end to petroleum levy
summary: Background of JI protests JI’s campaign against the petroleum levy intensified in August, when the party organised demonstrations and sit-ins across the country against rising fuel prices, inflation and what it described as an additional tax burden on consumers.
On September 12, the JI chief announced a long march towards Islamabad for September 20, warning that the party would intensify its campaign if the government did not abolish the levy.

The JI chief then gave the government 10 days to abolish the petroleum levy and provide meaningful relief to the inflation-hit public, warning that his party would resume its long march towards Islamabad in mid-November if its demands were not met.

stories.title: Ex-cricketer Usman Khawaja declines to confirm if Australia's bowlers were aware of 2018 ball-tampering plot
summary: Warner, who was banned from the team for a year and cast by Cricket Australia’s investigation as the chief architect of the plot, threw his weight behind Khawaja on Monday and said his account was 100 per cent accurate.

Cummins said in South Africa last month that he had spoken to Khawaja about his book and was not concerned about any potential fallout. “He just basically gave me the heads-up that he’s doing a book, and yeah, as always, no worries.
Australian media reported Khawaja pulled out of TV and radio interviews to promote his book following the TV interview.

stories.title: In pictures: Smog engulfs several Pakistani cities as air quality reaches ‘hazardous’ levels in Punjab
summary: Smog engulfed Pakistani skies on Wednesday as air quality continued to hover in the “hazardous” category, according to IQAir.

Of the major cities globally, IQAir ranked Lahore as the most polluted again on Wednesday, between 11am to noon, with an Air Quality Index (AQI) of 425, with levels above 300 being considered “hazardous”.
The Punjab government’s readings for the same hour showed that Muzaffargarh and Nankana Sahib’s AQI levels were at 500.

stories.title: PTI founder Imran Khan brought to Pims, undergoes eye procedure
summary: The hospital official added that, prior to the procedure, the former premier underwent a medical examination, including an ocular assessment. “His vital parameters were found to be normal.
Gohar added, “Regrettably, this order has remained unimplemented for nearly three months.” The former premier’s last reported hospital visit to Pims particularly for his eye ailment was in June.

On Aug 18, the Supreme Court directed the government to shift the jailed ex-premier to Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad, a day after the superintendent of the Adiala jail — where Imran is imprisoned — submitted a report to the SC on the ex-premier’s health condition.

stories.title: Pakistan fall short against Iran in 2027 AFC Under-17 Asian Cup qualifiers
summary: Iran broke the deadlock in the ninth minute when Amir Mohamed Zarei finished off an attack down Pakistan’s right flank.
Pakistan continued to press forward with Muhammad Essa causing problems through his pace and attacking runs on the right while Hasnain Ali remained influential on the opposite flank.
Despite their late efforts, Pakistan could not find a breakthrough and had to settle for a narrow defeat.

stories.title: Man Utd 'reach verbal agreement' with Pochettino
summary: Manchester United have reportedly reached a "verbal agreement in principle" with Mauricio Pochettino to replace Michael Carrick as their manager in a bid to revive the fortunes of the struggling English giants.

Carrick's position at Old Trafford has been the subject of intense speculation following United's worst start to a season in 40 years, leaving them languishing in the Premier League relegation zone after an eight-match winless run.
Carrick has presided over United's slide to 18th place -- their lowest position 10 games into a top-flight season since 1986/87 when they were 20th.

stories.title: India pollution monitors overwhelmed by toxic smog
summary: India’s air pollution monitors were overwhelmed this week by toxic smog so severe that concentrations exceeded their upper measurement limit, equivalent to 66 times the World Health Organisation’s recommended daily maximum, regulators said.

The admission comes after opposition politicians accused authorities of deliberately allowing gaps in official readings for several hours overnight Sunday into Monday, just as pollution surged with a barrage of fireworks for Diwali, the Hindu festival of lights.
Readings then hit 879 micrograms per cubic metre in the Mandir Marg locality, according to monitoring organisation IQAir, which cited data from a city government station.

stories.title: Hoax bomb alerts sent to schools in Italy, UK and Ireland in latest disruption
summary: Schools across Italy were evacuated on ‌Wednesday after around 6,300 of them received bomb warnings, the latest in a series of threats and cyberattacks around Europe against supermarkets, blood banks, air traffic and broadcasters.

Read: French officials blame Iran for refrigerator hacks, vow retaliation At least 300 schools in Italy were evacuated on Wednesday after receiving a bomb alert message, according to the Italian government.
The email received in Italy was signed "Mikhail Andropov, ​leader of the Vilayat of Misoginistan," according to a copy of the message seen by Reuters. “The (school) emails are public.

stories.title: Lahore court indicts eight in foreign woman rape case
summary: The case The statement of a 22-year-old Azerbaijani tourist, who told a Lahore court that she was confined, threatened, and sexually assaulted by three men before being allegedly pushed from a moving car.

She recorded her statement under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) before a judicial magistrate, naming Muhammad Ahmed Tanvir, Syed Mohsin Shah and Syed Ali Zain as the men she alleged had sexually assaulted her.
According to her statement, Ali Zain then threatened and blackmailed her, while the men told her she would have to drink alcohol with them before she could leave.

stories.title: Bethell ruled out of Australia tour
summary: England ​batter Jacob Bethell will miss the white-ball tour of Australia after a setback ‌in his recovery from a knee injury, the England ‌and Wales Cricket Board ⁠said ​on Wednesday.
"Jacob Bethell has been ruled out of the white-ball tour of Australia following a scan on his right knee," the ECB said.
England begin the three-match ⁠ODI series on Friday ​before playing five Twenty20 internationals.

stories.title: US judge rejects BBC bid to dismiss Trump defamation suit
summary: A federal judge allowed US President Donald Trump’s multi-billion dollar defamation suit against the BBC to proceed on Tuesday, rejecting a bid by the British broadcaster to dismiss the case.

Kuntz rejected the BBC’s bid to dismiss the defamation suit, but tossed the Florida protection law claim. “Whether President Trump can prove these claims and establish he sustained damages at summary judgement or trial is left for another day,” Kuntz wrote in a 40-page ruling.
The BBC documentary at issue spliced together two separate sections of Trump’s speech on January 6, 2021, making it appear that he had explicitly urged supporters to attack the US Capitol.

stories.title: ‘Harry Potter’ star Paapa Essiedu draws firm line on J.K. Rowling: ‘I don’t want to talk about Jo at all’
summary: Paapa Essiedu has addressed the controversy surrounding his involvement in HBO’s upcoming Harry Potter series, making his position on J.K.
The actor, who has been cast as Professor Severus Snape, told Vanity Fair that he did not want to discuss Rowling when asked about their reportedly differing views.
Since the announcement, Essiedu has faced racist abuse and death threats from individuals unhappy with the decision to cast a Black actor in the role.

stories.title: Elizabeth Olsen’s Marvel future takes unexpected turn after ‘VisionQuest’ finale
summary: Elizabeth Olsen’s Scarlet Witch is seemingly back in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, with the finale of VisionQuest setting up a major development ahead of Avengers: Doomsday.
According to Variety, the reveal follows speculation about Wanda’s involvement in the upcoming Marvel film.
Doom has also been linked to another powerful character, with a newly added post-credits scene in Avengers Endgame: Encore showing him kidnapping Mark Ruffalo’s Hulk.

stories.title: 10 policemen martyred, 18 terrorists killed in attack on Kohat police team
summary: It added that the police personnel martyred in the attack belonged to Kohat district and their sacrifices would always be remembered.
K-P Governor Faisal Karim Kundi strongly condemned the attack, expressing grief over the martyrdom of police personnel.

In a post on X, Samar described the attack on police personnel as highly regrettable and condemnable, saying that the nexus between Fitna al-Khawarij and criminal elements posed a serious threat to law and order.

stories.title: Dua Lipa, SZA and Tame Impala lead Coachella 2027 lineup
summary: The annual Valley Music and Arts Festival will return to the Empire Polo Club in Indio, California, across two weekends, running from April 9 to 11 and April 16 to 18.
The newly revealed bill also features several major performers, including Madonna, who is set to return to the festival’s Dance Tent.
The announcement follows SZA teasing the festival’s headline acts on social media before the official lineup was revealed, according to Variety.

stories.title: ADB announces $500m in contingent disaster financing for Pakistan
summary: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) on Wednesday approved $500 million in contingent disaster financing facilities for Pakistan to help the country withstand and respond to natural disasters, providing prompt budget support following eligible disaster events.
The ADB has also supported Pakistan's climate and disaster resilience efforts through earlier financing.

In April, the government also sought a further $1 billion in ADB financing under the programme's second tranche, with the proposed support covering disaster risk management, flood management and climate-resilient investment.

stories.title: China vows support for Cuba against sanctions, foreign interference amid US pressure
summary: China on Wednesday pledged unwavering support for Cuba against sanctions, blockades and foreign interference amid US pressure on Havana, as the two countries vowed to strengthen strategic ties and cooperation in multilateral forums.

Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi made the remarks during talks in Beijing with his Cuban counterpart Bruno Rodriguez Parrilla, who is visiting as a special envoy of Cuba's party and government, according to a statement published on China's Foreign Ministry website.
Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi held talks with Cuban Minister of Foreign Affairs Bruno Rodriguez Parrilla in Beijing on Wednesday.

stories.title: Workers across Spain stage first general strike in 14 years as anger rages over housing
summary: Spanish workers went on a general strike on Wednesday, enduring stormy weather to set up picket lines in a mass protest against the country's housing affordability crisis less than three weeks before a snap general election.

Unions said participation in the strike was uneven across Spain, with the strongest support in coastal regions including the Cantabrian coast, Catalonia, Andalusia and parts of the Mediterranean, where housing pressures have been particularly acute.
But union leaders and many of the protesters have said they also hold the central government responsible for the housing crisis, as well as for Spain's second fatal train crash this year.

stories.title: Fire destroys hotel’s hall during Diwali celebration in Sukkur
summary: SUKKUR: A wedding hall was destroyed when firecrackers caused a big fire inside during a function held to celebrate Diwali on Monday night.
Management of the hotel, located near the City Point Bypass, confirmed to local reporters that the blaze was caused by the fireworks set off during the celebration.
According to the hotel staff, people started rushing to safety as soon as the fire intensified.

stories.title: Jamie Dornan opens up about carrying legacy of beloved ‘Lord of the Rings’ character
summary: Jamie Dornan has spoken about the emotional moment he discovered he would play Aragorn in The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum, admitting that the casting news brought him to tears.
Dornan described the opportunity as a dream and an honour, particularly because Aragorn remains one of the franchise's most admired characters.
"Aragorn will always be just Viggo," Dornan said in an earlier interview with L'Officiel.

stories.title: Imran's BP at 'frightening level' but ex-PM still 'alert and strong', Latif Khosa says after hours-long Adiala meeting
summary: Today nearly Three (3) hours long meeting with Imran Khan Sb & Bushra Bibi was allowed by Adyala Jail Authorities.
In April 2026, Barrister Salman Safdar met Imran for a 60-minute legal consultation on the IHC’s orders, but Bushra Bibi was not brought in to join the meeting.
However, Safdar was not allowed to meet both his clients again until November 2, when jail authorities facilitated a 40-minute meeting with Imran and Bushra Bibi.

stories.title: Jirga in Mirpur Bhutto ends 14-year-old hostility involving five communities
summary: After prolonged consultations, the Jirga pronounced its ruling, according to which a fine of Rs9.5 million was imposed on the side comprising the Bhutto, Kuriya and Narejo communities.

Chandio-Magsi feud Another Jirga, held in Qambar town, settled an old dispute between the Chandio and Magsi communities by imposing heavy fines on both the sides and ordering them to stop further bloodshed.
Both sides accepted the ruling and part of the fine amount, Rs500,000, was deposited with the Jirga on behalf of the Magsi side.
